title: Tensor-power and Proj-twist section localizations agree
statement: Let $S=\bigoplus_{d\ge0}S_d$ be a nonnegatively graded commutative ring and $X=\operatorname{Proj}(S)$ [def-pc-proj]. Assume that $X$ is covered by the standard opens $D_+(f)$ with $f\in S_1$. Let $\mathcal F$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Put $\mathcal O_X(n)=\widetilde{S(n)}$ [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], $\mathcal F(n)=\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal O_X(n)$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and $N=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\Gamma(X,\mathcal F(n))$, with the $S$-action given by canonical sections and the unital associative twist multiplication maps of [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor]. Put $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$, an invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module], $B=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Gamma(X,L^{\otimes n})$, and $P=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbf Z}\Gamma(X,\mathcal F\otimes L^{\otimes n})$, with negative powers interpreted using the dual of $L$. The canonical multiplication identifications $\beta_n:L^{\otimes n}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal O_X(n)$, for every $n\in\mathbf Z$, identify the graded $S$-module $P$ (by restriction of scalars along the canonical map $S\to B$) with $N$. For every $f\in S_1$ let $s\in\Gamma(X,L)$ be its canonical section, and define $X_s=\{x:s\notin\mathfrak m_xL_x\}$. Then $X_s=D_+(f)$, and $s$ freely generates $L|_{D_+(f)}$. The identifications induce an $S_{(f)}$-linear isomorphism $\theta_f:N_{(f)}\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{(s)}$ sending $t/f^a$ to $\beta_a^{-1}(t)/s^a$ for $a\ge0$ and $t\in N_a$, where $\beta_a^{-1}$ on sections includes the identity on $\mathcal F$. Here $N_{(f)}$ and $P_{(s)}$ mean the degree-zero parts of the respective homogeneous localizations; equality of two fractions with denominators of exponents $a,b$ is the common-power relation $f^c(f^bt-f^au)=0$ for some $c\ge0$, transported to the same relation with $s$. Under $X_s=D_+(f)$, restriction followed by division by $s^a$ composed with $\theta_f$ is exactly $t/f^a\mapsto t|_{D_+(f)}\otimes f^{-a}$. No quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness, or quasi-coherence is assumed in this comparison.

source.place: Tag 0AG5 (lemma-proj-quasi-coherent), proof: the identification of twisted-section homogeneous localization with invertible-section localization, specialized to d=1; its twist and nonvanishing identifications come from constructions.tex lemma-apply-modules and lemma-principal-open.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-standard-proj-twist-tensor] with the given degree-one cover. It supplies invertibility of every $\mathcal O_X(n)$ and the isomorphisms $\mu_{a,b}$, including their unit and associativity laws and their fraction multiplication formula. In particular $L=\mathcal O_X(1)$ is invertible. Use the evaluation isomorphism $L\otimes L^\vee\simeq\mathcal O_X$ of [lem-pc-tensor-dual-invertible] to interpret negative powers. All tensor associators and unitors below are those of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed].

source.place: Tags 01MS (lemma-when-invertible) and 01MT (lemma-apply-modules), multiplication isomorphisms; negative powers use the dual evaluation.

proof.text: Fix $g\in S_1$, $U_g=D_+(g)$, and $n\in\mathbf Z$. On each positive-degree standard open $V=D_+(h)\subseteq U_g$, [lem-weil-pbc-proj-standard-open-inclusion] makes $g$ a homogeneous unit in $S_h$. By [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], the maps $\mathcal O_X(V)=(S_h)_0\to(S_h)_n=\mathcal O_X(n)(V)$, $a\mapsto ag^n$, and $x\mapsto g^{-n}x$ are inverse linear maps. Both commute with localization restrictions. These $V$ form a basis of $U_g$, so [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-morphism-on-basis] extends them to inverse sheaf maps on $U_g$. Denote the resulting frame by $g^n$, also for negative $n$; $g^0=1$. For $n=1$ it is the restriction of the canonical section of $L$, because that section has fractions $g/1$ on every standard open.

source.place: Tag 01MS (lemma-when-invertible), proof: multiplication by g^n after inverting g; Tag 01MM canonical homogeneous sections.

proof.text: Write $E_n=L^{\otimes n}$, with $E_0=\mathcal O_X$. The frame $g$ on $U_g$ has dual frame $g^\vee$ with $g^\vee(g)=1$. Its tensor powers, or the powers of $g^\vee$ for $n<0$, give frames $e_{g,n}$ of $E_n|_{U_g}$: tensor the trivialization and its inverse, and use the unitors; for the dual use evaluation. Define $\beta_{n,g}$ by $ae_{g,n}\mapsto ag^n$. On $U_g\cap U_h$, the unit $r=g/h$ satisfies $g=rh$, hence $g^\vee=r^{-1}h^\vee$ and $e_{g,n}=r^ne_{h,n}$ for every integer $n$. In the localized graded ring one also has $g^n=r^nh^n$. Thus $\beta_{n,g}$ and $\beta_{n,h}$ agree on overlaps. Restrict a section to the cover, apply these maps, and glue; their inverse maps glue by the same equations. This constructs $\beta_n:E_n\simeq\mathcal O_X(n)$ globally. For $n\ge0$ it is the iterated canonical multiplication map: induction starts with $\beta_0=1$, $\beta_1=1$, and the successor sends $e_{g,n}\otimes g$ to $g^{n+1}$. For $n<0$ it is its dual counterpart, as $g^n g^{-n}=1$.

source.place: Tag 01MT (lemma-apply-modules), tensor-power identification; Tag 01MS frames. The overlap and negative-power details are written out here.

proof.text: The maps $\beta_n$ respect multiplication in all integer degrees. On any open contained in $U_g$, multiplication of the tensor frames is $e_{g,a}e_{g,b}=e_{g,a+b}$, including mixed signs since evaluation pairs $g$ with $g^\vee$ to $1$. Multiplication of the twist frames is $g^ag^b=g^{a+b}$ by the fraction formula. Both maps are bilinear between locally free rank-one sheaves, so these equations on their frames prove their equality. The degree-zero map is the unit identification. Consequently $\phi:S\to B$ sends $v\in S_e$ to $\beta_e^{-1}(v)$ and is a unital graded ring map. Put $\gamma_n=\Gamma(X,1_{\mathcal F}\otimes\beta_n):P_n\simeq N_n$. Locally every section of $\mathcal F\otimes E_n$ is uniquely $z\otimes e_{g,n}$, by the tensor unitor and the frame. If $v|_{U_g}=qg^e$, the two actions on this section both give $qz\otimes g^{n+e}$. Restriction to the cover and sheaf separation prove $\gamma_{n+e}(\phi(v)p)=v\gamma_n(p)$. Taking direct sums gives the asserted graded $S$-module isomorphism $\gamma:P\simeq N$.

source.place: Tag 01MT and equations equation-multiply, equation-multiply-on-sheaf: multiplicativity checked on local frames, also after tensoring an arbitrary module sheaf.

proof.text: Every $\mathcal O_X(n)$ is invertible and every $\mu_{a,b}$ is an isomorphism by step 1. Therefore the open $W_1$ in [lem-trf-proj-twist-section-basic-open] is all of $X$. Apply that node with $A=S$, $d=n=1$, $U=X$, and the given $f\in S_1$. It gives $X_s=D_+(f)$, with the stated stalk definition of the nonvanishing locus. Step 2 with $g=f$, $n=1$ says that $s=f/1$ freely generates $L$ on this open. In particular its powers are the frames $e_{f,a}$, and $\beta_a(e_{f,a})=f^a$.

source.place: Tag 01MV (lemma-principal-open), with W_1=X supplied by Tag 01MT. No compactness hypothesis is used.

proof.text: Let $\delta_n=\gamma_n^{-1}$. Step 4 gives $\delta_{n+1}(ft)=s\delta_n(t)$, hence by induction $\delta_{n+c}(f^ct)=s^c\delta_n(t)$ for $c\ge0$. Define $\theta_f(t/f^a)=\delta_a(t)/s^a$. It is well defined: for $t\in N_a$, $u\in N_b$, the relation $f^c(f^bt-f^au)=0$ is sent by the additive isomorphism $\delta_{a+b+c}$ to $s^c(s^b\delta_a(t)-s^a\delta_b(u))=0$. Conversely $\gamma_{a+b+c}$ takes the latter relation back to the former. Thus the two fraction relations are equivalent, without cancelling any power. The inverse map is $p/s^a\mapsto\gamma_a(p)/f^a$. These formulas give a bijection on the degree-zero localizations and are precisely the formula involving $\beta_a^{-1}$ in the statement.

source.place: Tag 0AG5 (lemma-proj-quasi-coherent), proof: the graded-section localization identification, d=1; the ordinary common-power fraction relation is explicit in the statement of this item.

proof.text: The bijection is additive: the numerator of $t/f^a+u/f^b$ over $f^{a+b}$ is $f^bt+f^au$, and its image under $\delta_{a+b}$ is $s^b\delta_a(t)+s^a\delta_b(u)$, the numerator of the corresponding sum over $s^{a+b}$. Define the coefficient-ring map $S_{(f)}\to B_{(s)}$ by $v/f^b\mapsto\phi(v)/s^b$ for $v\in S_b$; the ring-map law and $\phi(f)=s$ send its common-power relation to that in $B_{(s)}$, so it is well defined. Equip $P_{(s)}$ with this $S_{(f)}$-action. Step 4 gives $\delta_{a+b}(vt)=\phi(v)\delta_a(t)$, whence $\theta_f((v/f^b)(t/f^a))=(\phi(v)/s^b)\theta_f(t/f^a)$. This proves $S_{(f)}$-linearity and makes the inverse linear as well.

source.place: Tag 0AG5 (lemma-proj-quasi-coherent), proof: equality as localized modules, with addition and coefficient action written out.

proof.text: On $U=X_s=D_+(f)$ define division by $s^a$ using the frame $e_{f,a}$: the map $\mathcal F|_U\to(\mathcal F\otimes E_a)|_U$, $z\mapsto z\otimes e_{f,a}$, is an isomorphism. The division map on fractions is well defined, since after restriction to $U$ its common-power relation may be divided by the frame $s^{a+b+c}$. Step 3 gives $\beta_a(e_{f,a})=f^a$, so dividing $\delta_a(t)|_U$ by $s^a$ is exactly contracting $t|_U\in\Gamma(U,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal O_X(a))$ against the inverse frame $f^{-a}$. Its value is $t|_U\otimes f^{-a}$ under the canonical multiplication and unit identification. This proves the final compatibility. No assertion of bijectivity of this restriction-and-division map was used. The construction uses only the degree-one open cover, valid also when it is infinite; it applies to arbitrary $\mathcal F$, without quasi-coherence, quasi-compactness, or quasi-separatedness.

source.place: Tag 0AG5 (lemma-proj-quasi-coherent), comparison formula, together with constructions.tex Tag 01MS inverse frames; only the formal comparison part of that proof is used.
